lines.text: 公司换了一套新的电脑系统，信息部规定：登录密码每个月必须换一次。
lines.py: gōng sī huàn le yí tào xīn de diàn nǎo xì tǒng, xìn xī bù guī dìng: dēng lù mì mǎ měi gè yuè bì xū huàn yí cì.
lines.en: The company switches to a new computer system, and IT rules that login passwords must be changed once a month.

lines.text: 新密码不能少于十二位，要有大写字母、小写字母、数字和符号，而且不能跟以前用过的一样。

lines.en: New passwords must be at least twelve characters long, with capitals, lower-case letters, numbers and symbols, and can't be the same as any used before.

lines.text: 杰克不想把密码写在纸上，想了一个晚上，想出了一个一举两得的办法：每个月用一个新学的成语当密码。
lines.py: Jié kè bù xiǎng bǎ mì mǎ xiě zài zhǐ shàng, xiǎng le yí gè wǎn shang, xiǎng chū le yí gè yì jǔ liǎng de de bàn fǎ: měi gè yuè yòng yí gè xīn xué de chéng yǔ dāng mì mǎ.
lines.en: Jack doesn't want to write his password down anywhere, and after an evening's thought he comes up with a way to kill two birds with one stone: every month, he'll use a chengyu he's just learned as his password.

lines.en: For example, in February he's just learned hua she tian zu, "drawing legs on a snake", so he uses its pinyin with the first letter in capitals, followed by the month and an exclamation mark.

lines.text: 三月是“守株待兔”，四月是“对牛弹琴”，五月是“半途而废”……一年下来，他一共用掉了十一个成语。

lines.en: March is "waiting by the tree stump for a rabbit", April "playing the lute to a cow", May "giving up halfway"... by the end of the year, he's used up eleven chengyu.
